Suraz Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Suraż, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are recorded in Suraż from the 16th century, though the community only developed significantly in the 19th; population peaked at 386 in 1897, declining to just 86 by 1931 as most later residents were killed during WWII. This cemetery, per unconfirmed sources founded in 1865, was formally closed by Poland in 1967, with documentation noting a last burial in 1943. A 1987 government survey found tombstones destroyed and graves obliterated, at which point authorities considered building a slaughterhouse on the grounds. Two surviving matzevot are held at the Museum of Archaeology and Ethnography in Suraż.
